md_name: Single-cell amplified genome workflow for uncultured marine microbes
md_description: This DAG represents the experimental and computational workflow used to generate single-cell amplified genomes from uncultured marine microbes. It begins with marine environmental samples, isolates individual cells by microfluidics, lyses and amplifies their genomes by multiple displacement amplification, then sequences and assembles the resulting DNA. Assembly, annotation, and quality assessment software produce genome reconstructions and metrics that are integrated into a final SAG metadata table for downstream ecological analysis of microbial genomic diversity and roles.

marine_microbial_community_sample.reasoning: This is the root Entity node, so I included only intrinsic sample identity and origin fields: what the environmental sample is, where it came from, and its collection context. I excluded all process, capture, signal, and derivative details because those belong to downstream nodes (isolation, sequencing, assembly, etc.). I also avoided sample/subject/experiment identifiers if they might already be generated elsewhere; since no already_generated list was provided here, I kept the schema limited to core root-level entity descriptors that would not duplicate downstream workflow metadata.

md_schema.descr: Categorical descriptor of the environmental material represented by this root entity; use this at the sample-record level before any cell isolation or processing. Typical values distinguish seawater, marine microbial community, or similar marine environmental matrices.

Free-text description of the marine source environment for the sample, recorded at collection time before any processing; include the general habitat such as coastal ocean, open ocean, estuary, or deep sea, and the broad location name if available.

Geographic collection location for the marine sample, recorded at the original sampling event. Use a human-readable place name or coordinates example such as '37.7749 N, 122.4194 W' or 'North Atlantic Ocean'.

Sampling depth in meters below the water surface at which the marine sample was collected, recorded at collection time before any processing. Typical values range from 0 to several thousand meters depending on the expedition.
Date when the marine environmental sample was collected, in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Record the date of the original field sampling event, not downstream processing dates.

Categorical descriptor of the sample state immediately after collection and before cell isolation or lysis. Use this to indicate whether the sample was processed fresh or preserved for later workflow steps.

Salinity of the marine source water or sample matrix in practical salinity units (PSU), measured or recorded at collection time. Typical marine values are approximately 30-40 PSU, with estuarine samples often lower.
In situ or collection-time temperature of the marine sample in degrees Celsius, recorded before any processing. Typical marine environmental ranges are approximately -2 to 30 C depending on habitat.

Short narrative description of the original marine community sample, including any relevant collection notes that define the entity itself before workflow processing, such as seawater fraction, filtration status if intrinsic to collection, or observed microbial community context.

microfluidic_single_cell_isolation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the isolation protocol and device-operation details: microfluidic method, chip/device configuration, trapping/sorting settings, and operator/platform identifiers. I excluded sample-origin fields because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded downstream output properties of the isolated cell because those belong to the isolated_single_cell Entity. No already_generated list was provided in this turn, so I avoided only territory overlap by staying within the process layer.

md_schema.descr: Categorical label for the microfluidic cell isolation approach used to capture single uncultured microbial cells from the marine community sample. Record this at the time the isolation process is performed; examples include droplet-based sorting, microfluidic trapping, or flow-based single-cell capture.
Name of the manufacturer of the microfluidic instrument or platform used for single-cell isolation, recorded for the process configuration. Example: 'Dolomite', 'Fluidigm', or another vendor name.
Model name or number of the microfluidic platform used for cell isolation, recorded with the process settings. Example format: 'Model X' or 'C1 system'.

Serial number of the microfluidic instrument used for isolation, recorded to identify the exact hardware instance used in the session. Use the vendor-assigned serial identifier string, for example 'SN123456'.

Identifier for the microfluidic chip, cartridge, or disposable device used during the single-cell isolation step. Record the device ID or lot-specific identifier used in this isolation session, for example 'chip_07' or a barcode string.

Operating pressure in pounds per square inch used by the microfluidic sorting or trapping system during cell isolation. Record the setpoint used during the isolation session; typical values depend on platform and often fall in the low-to-mid tens of psi.

Flow rate in microliters per minute used to move the sample through the microfluidic isolation device during trapping or sorting. Record the instrument setpoint during the isolation session; typical values are platform-specific and often range from fractions to tens of uL/min.

Boolean flag indicating whether successful recovery of an individual cell was confirmed during the isolation process, using the workflow's operational criteria. Set true when the isolation session produced a verified single-cell recovery.
Free-text notes about the isolation run, including operator observations, deviations, or any microfluidic handling details relevant to the process but not captured by the structured fields.

isolated_single_cell.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the isolated cell itself, so I included intrinsic properties of the recovered single cell and its provenance from the marine sample. I excluded isolation device settings and operator parameters because those belong to the upstream microfluidic isolation Process, and I excluded lysis/amplification/sequence outputs because those are downstream nodes. I also avoided duplicating any sample-level identifiers or environmental origin fields that would already be set on the root sample entity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the individually isolated microbial cell, assigned after microfluidic isolation and used to track the same cell through lysis, amplification, sequencing, and downstream analysis. Use a stable string example such as 'cell_0001' or a barcode-linked ID.

Identifier linking this isolated cell back to the original marine community sample from which it was recovered. Record the parent sample ID as a string example such as 'sample_A12'; this is the provenance link, not a new sample identifier.

Categorical status of the isolated cell at the point it is handed off to downstream genomic processing. Use this to indicate whether the cell was recovered intact, partially damaged, or otherwise noted by the workflow.

Free-text observational notes on the isolated cell's morphology or appearance, if assessed during or immediately after isolation. Record visible features such as approximate shape, size impression, or unusual characteristics, without including instrument settings.

Free-text description of how the isolation was verified as a single cell, recorded at the entity handoff point after microfluidic isolation and before lysis. Examples include microscopic confirmation, fluorescence check, or imaging-based verification.

Estimated diameter of the isolated cell in micrometers, if measured or inferred at the time of isolation. Typical microbial single-cell values are often in the sub-micrometer to several-micrometer range, depending on taxon.

Optional preliminary taxonomic hint for the isolated cell, based on morphology or rapid screening at the time of isolation. Record as a free-text or standardized label only if an early assignment was made; do not use this as a final annotation.

Categorical description of how the isolated cell was held between isolation and downstream lysis, if applicable. Use this to capture the entity's immediate post-isolation state, not the lysis protocol.

cell_lysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only lysis protocol parameters and reagents used to break open the isolated cell, plus a concise process outcome indicator. I excluded upstream entity properties of the isolated cell and downstream properties of the lysed material or amplified DNA, since those belong to neighboring Entity nodes. I also avoided repeating any platform/software fields because this process is wet-lab and not computational; no already_generated list was provided here, so I limited the schema to the process territory only.

md_schema.descr: Categorical label for the lysis approach applied to the isolated single cell before whole-genome amplification. Record the method used at the time of lysis; examples include chemical, enzymatic, thermal, or combined lysis approaches.

Free-text description of the lysis buffer or chemistry used during the cell lysis step, including key components and approximate concentrations if known. Example: 'alkaline buffer with detergent and reducing agent'.

Incubation temperature in degrees Celsius used during the lysis treatment, measured as the setpoint applied to the isolated cell during lysis. Typical values depend on protocol and may range from ambient to elevated temperatures.

Duration in minutes that the isolated cell was exposed to the lysis conditions. Record the actual protocol time applied during this process step; typical values may range from minutes to hours depending on chemistry.

Categorical process-quality indicator describing whether the lysis step appeared to succeed in releasing material suitable for downstream amplification. Use this at the end of the lysis process, before MDA begins.
Manufacturer or vendor of the principal lysis reagent kit or chemistry used in this process, if applicable. Example: 'Qiagen', 'Thermo Fisher', or a protocol-specific supplier name.
Lot or batch number of the lysis reagent or kit used during the lysis process, recorded to support reproducibility and traceability. Use the vendor-assigned lot string such as 'lot_2024-05A'.
Free-text notes describing any deviations, observations, or handling details during the lysis step that are relevant to the process but not captured by structured fields.

lysed_single_cell.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included intrinsic post-lysis material properties: that the single cell has been lysed, whether recoverable genomic DNA is present, and simple material state/handling descriptors. I excluded lysis protocol variables because those belong to the upstream cell_lysis Process, and I excluded amplification inputs/outputs because those belong to the downstream MDA process and amplified DNA entity. No already_generated list was provided here, so I kept the schema focused on non-duplicative entity-level descriptors for the lysed material.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the lysed single-cell material after the lysis step, used to track the same sample material into whole-genome amplification. Example format: 'lysed_cell_0001'.
Boolean flag indicating whether genomic DNA was judged to be available from the lysed cell for downstream whole-genome amplification at the point this entity was recorded.

Estimated or measured lysate volume in microliters immediately after lysis, recorded for the post-lysis material state. Typical values are often in the single-digit to tens of microliters depending on protocol.
Categorical description of how the lysed cell material was held before amplification. Record the immediate post-lysis storage state, such as direct handoff to MDA, chilled storage, or frozen storage.

Free-text notes describing the appearance or handling of the lysed material, recorded after lysis and before amplification. Include any visible residue, clarity, or unusual handling issues relevant to the entity state.
Identifier linking this lysed material back to the isolated single-cell record from which it was produced. Use the pre-existing cell ID string, for example 'cell_0001', to maintain provenance.

multiple_displacement_amplification.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only MDA protocol parameters, reagents, incubation settings, and a process-level success/quality indicator. I excluded properties of the lysed input material and the amplified DNA output, since those belong to the upstream and downstream Entity nodes respectively. I also included the software/agent identity only in a process-appropriate way if it were computational, but here the agent is the wet-lab MDA protocol, so no software fields were added. No already_generated list was provided in this turn, so I avoided overlap by keeping the schema strictly within the amplification process territory.

md_schema.descr: Name of the DNA polymerase or amplification enzyme used for multiple displacement amplification, recorded at the time the MDA process was executed. Example: phi29 polymerase or a vendor-specific kit enzyme name.

Total reaction volume in microliters used for the MDA reaction, recorded as the set up for the amplification step. Typical values are often in the single-digit to tens of microliters depending on protocol.

Incubation temperature in degrees Celsius used during multiple displacement amplification, recorded as the reaction setpoint during the process. MDA is commonly run at a constant temperature, often around 30 C.
Duration in hours that the MDA reaction was allowed to proceed, recorded for the amplification process step. Typical durations may range from a few hours to overnight incubation.
Categorical description of the primer chemistry used for MDA, recorded during reaction setup. Use this to distinguish random primers or kit-specific priming approaches.
Manufacturer or vendor of the amplification kit or reagent system used for MDA, recorded for process traceability. Example: 'Qiagen', 'Meridian', or a similar supplier name.
Lot or batch number of the MDA kit or key reagent used in the reaction, recorded to support reproducibility and troubleshooting. Use the vendor-assigned lot string such as 'lot_24B07'.

Categorical indicator summarizing whether the MDA reaction generated sufficient amplified DNA for downstream sequencing and assembly, recorded at the end of the process. This is a process-level outcome, not a property of the amplified DNA entity.

amplified_sag_dna.reasoning: This is an Entity node for the amplified DNA product, so I included intrinsic properties of the material itself: identity/provenance, concentration, total yield, storage, and a simple material-quality note. I excluded MDA protocol settings because those belong to the upstream process, and I excluded sequencing/capture settings because those belong downstream. No already_generated list was provided here, so I kept the schema focused on the amplified DNA entity and avoided repeating process-level fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the amplified single-cell genomic DNA product generated by MDA, used as the sequencing input record. Example format: 'amplified_sag_dna_0001'.
Identifier linking this amplified DNA entity back to the lysed single-cell material from which it was produced. Use the parent material ID string, for example 'lysed_cell_0001'.

Concentration of the amplified SAG DNA in nanograms per microliter, measured after amplification and before sequencing library preparation or sequencing input handoff. Typical values can vary widely depending on MDA yield.
Total yield of amplified DNA in nanograms, measured or estimated after completion of MDA and before downstream processing. Record the total mass recovered from the reaction product.
Categorical description of how the amplified DNA was stored after generation and before sequencing. Use this to capture the material state, such as refrigerated, frozen, or immediate use.

Free-text notes on the quality or apparent purity of the amplified DNA product, recorded after amplification and before sequencing. Include any observations such as visible high-molecular-weight product, suspected contamination, or unusual viscosity.

Recovered volume in microliters of the amplified DNA product available for downstream sequencing input, measured after amplification and any cleanup. Typical values depend on the MDA protocol and recovery step.

sequencing_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included the sequencing session and instrument configuration: platform, manufacturer/model/serial, library/input settings, run parameters, and operator-controlled acquisition settings. I excluded sample or amplified-DNA intrinsic properties because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded file-level read properties because those belong to the downstream raw_sag_reads Signal node. No already_generated list was provided here, so I avoided only territory overlap by staying in the capture layer and including instrument-identifying details as required.

md_schema.descr: Categorical label for the sequencing technology used to capture the amplified SAG DNA into raw reads. Record the platform at the time of the sequencing session; examples include Illumina short-read sequencing or other instrument classes.
Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session, recorded as part of the instrument configuration. Example: 'Illumina', 'Thermo Fisher', or another vendor name.
Sequencer model name or number used for the sequencing session, recorded with the capture configuration. Example format: 'NovaSeq 6000' or 'MiSeq'.

Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for the run, recorded to identify the exact hardware instance that captured the SAG DNA. Use the vendor-assigned serial identifier string, for example 'SN123456'.

Identifier for the individual sequencing run or lane used to generate raw SAG reads from the amplified DNA. Use the run- or lane-specific string assigned by the instrument or lab workflow, for example 'run_2024_08_01' or 'lane_3'.

Configured read length in base pairs for the sequencing capture session, measured as the planned or achieved read length setting for the run. Typical values depend on platform and chemistry, such as 150 bp paired-end on Illumina.

Amount of amplified SAG DNA input to sequencing library preparation or loading, in nanograms, recorded at the capture session boundary. This is the material loaded for sequencing, not a property of the output reads.
Version or name of the sequencing reagent kit used in the capture session, recorded for instrument configuration and reproducibility. Example: 'v2 chemistry' or a vendor kit name.

Cluster density in thousands per square millimeter, when applicable to short-read sequencing platforms, recorded as a run-quality/acquisition parameter. Use the instrument-reported value if available; otherwise leave unreported for non-applicable platforms.
Free-text notes describing the sequencing session, including any run deviations, loading issues, or acquisition details relevant to the capture configuration but not to the raw file itself.

raw_sag_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw-data artefact properties: file format, file size, read counts, read length/quality summaries, storage location, and basic technical integrity flags. I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded any biological interpretation or assembly-related metrics because those belong downstream to process/derivative nodes. No already_generated list was provided here, so I focused on non-overlapping signal-level descriptors needed to locate, validate, and reuse the raw read files.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw SAG read data artifact produced by sequencing, recorded for the raw signal file itself. Typical values include FASTQ or related sequencer-export formats; note the format as stored in the dataset.

File size of the raw read data artifact in bytes, measured for the stored sequencing output file(s) after generation. Use the on-disk size of the raw signal record, typically ranging from megabytes to gigabytes depending on run scale.
Total number of reads contained in the raw SAG sequencing data file, recorded as a property of the raw signal artifact after sequencing export. This is a file-level count, not a biological count.
Total number of bases in the raw SAG reads, in base pairs, calculated from the raw signal artifact contents. Use the value associated with the stored raw data file, not downstream filtered reads.

Mean read length in base pairs for the raw sequencing reads, measured from the raw data artifact after sequencing capture. Typical values depend on platform and chemistry, such as around 150 bp for short-read runs.

Average base-call quality score summary for the raw read artifact, recorded as a technical quality metric of the file contents. Use the file-level mean or comparable summary reported for the raw data.

Path, URI, or accession pointing to the stored raw SAG read file(s), recorded for the signal artifact location. Example: a local path such as '/data/run1/sample.fastq.gz' or a repository accession string.
Checksum or hash for the raw read file used to verify file integrity and identity, recorded as a technical signal-level control. Example formats include MD5 or SHA256 digest strings.
Boolean flag indicating whether the raw sequencing file passed basic integrity validation at the time of ingestion, such as checksum verification or file readability checks.

read_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational trimming/filtering workflow settings and software agent details, plus a process-level output quality indicator. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded processed-read file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also followed the rule to place software name/version/repository on the Process node, since this is a computational operation. No already_generated list was provided here, so I avoided overlap by staying strictly in the read-processing process territory.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to trim and filter the raw SAG reads, recorded for the computational process that transforms raw reads into processed reads. Example: 'fastp', 'Trimmomatic', or a custom workflow name.

Version of the read-processing software used in the trimming and filtering step, recorded at run time for reproducibility. Use the exact release or commit version string, for example '0.23.4' or 'v1.2.0'.

Repository location or reference for the read-processing software used in the computational step, recorded to identify the codebase. Example: a GitHub URL, package source, or internal repository identifier.
Boolean flag indicating whether sequencing adapter trimming was performed during read processing. Record this at the time the computational filtering step is executed.

Phred quality threshold used for trimming low-quality bases or reads during processing, recorded as the configured cutoff for the filtering step. Typical values often fall between 15 and 30 depending on stringency.

Minimum read length in base pairs required for a read to be retained after trimming/filtering, recorded as the processing cutoff. Typical values depend on downstream assembly requirements and sequencing platform.
Boolean flag indicating whether reads were screened to remove suspected contaminant sequences during processing, such as adapter, phiX, or host carryover if applicable.

Fraction of raw reads retained after processing, recorded as a process-level efficiency metric after trimming and filtering. Use a value between 0 and 1 summarizing how much input data passed the filters.
Free-text notes describing special handling, exceptions, or observations during read trimming and filtering that are relevant to the computational process but not captured by structured settings.

processed_sag_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only processed-read artefact properties: file format, file size, counts and length summaries after filtering, storage location, and technical integrity/retention descriptors. I excluded read-processing software and thresholds because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded assembly parameters because those belong downstream. No already_generated list was provided here, so I kept the schema focused on the processed-read file as a reusable signal artefact and avoided duplicating upstream capture or process metadata.

md_schema.descr: File format of the quality-filtered SAG read data artifact after trimming and filtering, recorded for the processed signal file itself. Typical values include FASTQ or related storage formats.

File size of the processed read data artifact in bytes, measured for the stored file(s) after read processing. Use the on-disk size of the processed signal record, typically smaller than the raw read file.

Total number of reads retained in the processed SAG data after trimming and filtering, recorded as a property of the processed signal artifact. This reflects the output file contents, not the raw input count.
Total number of bases in the processed SAG reads, in base pairs, calculated from the filtered read artifact. Use the contents of the stored processed data file, not the raw reads.
Mean read length in base pairs for the processed reads after filtering and trimming, measured from the processed signal artifact. Typical values depend on the retained read population and platform.
Average base-call quality score summary for the processed read artifact, recorded as a technical quality metric of the filtered data file. Use the file-level summary reported for the processed reads.

Path, URI, or accession pointing to the stored processed SAG read file(s), recorded for the signal artifact location. Example: '/data/processed/sample_trimmed.fastq.gz' or a repository accession string.
Checksum or hash for the processed read file used to verify file integrity and identity, recorded as a signal-level control. Example formats include MD5 or SHA256 digest strings.
Boolean flag indicating whether the processed read file passed basic integrity validation at ingestion, such as checksum verification or file readability checks.

genome_assembly.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only assembly workflow parameters and the assembler software identity/version, plus a process-level quality summary. I excluded processed-read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded contig/assembly result properties because those belong to the downstream sag_assembly Derivative node. I also followed the rule to place software name, version, and repository on the Process node. No already_generated list was provided here, so I stayed strictly within the assembly process territory and avoided duplicating downstream assembly metrics.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used to reconstruct contigs from processed SAG reads, recorded for the computational assembly process. Example: 'SPAdes', 'MEGAHIT', or another assembler name.
Version or release identifier of the assembler used in the genome assembly step, recorded at run time for reproducibility. Use the exact version string, such as '3.15.5' or a commit tag.
Repository location or reference for the assembly software used in this process, recorded to identify the codebase. Example: a GitHub URL, package source, or internal repository identifier.

Categorical description of the assembly strategy used for the SAG genome reconstruction, recorded during the assembly process. Use this to distinguish single-cell-aware, metagenomic, or hybrid approaches.
Comma-separated list or textual description of the k-mer sizes used by the assembler during the genome assembly process. Example: '21,33,55,77' or a comparable run-time parameter string.
Minimum contig length in base pairs retained or targeted during assembly, recorded as a process parameter for the assembler. Typical values depend on the workflow and downstream quality criteria.
Number of processed reads supplied to the assembler for this assembly run, recorded as a process-level input summary. This is a computational input count, not a signal-file property.
Free-text notes describing assembly-specific settings, deviations, or run observations that are relevant to the reconstruction process but not captured by structured fields.

Categorical indicator summarizing the apparent success of the assembly process, recorded at the end of genome reconstruction. This is a process-level outcome and not the final assembly object's quality metric.

sag_assembly.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed assembly-result properties: assembly identity, contig set dimensions, basic contiguity statistics, completeness/contamination-style summary metrics if available as computed outputs, and the location/checksum of the derived assembly artifact. I excluded assembler settings because those belong to the upstream genome_assembly Process, and I excluded annotation/quality-assessment pipeline fields because those belong to downstream derivative or process nodes. No already_generated list was provided here, so I focused on the assembly object as the computed result and avoided duplicating process parameters.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed SAG genome assembly or contig set, assigned after the assembly process completes. Example format: 'sag_assembly_0001'.
Identifier linking this assembly back to the processed SAG reads used as input for reconstruction. Use the parent signal ID string, for example 'processed_sag_reads_0001'.
Total number of contigs in the assembled SAG genome, calculated for the derivative assembly object after reconstruction. This is a basic assembly-size descriptor.
Total length of all contigs in the SAG assembly, in base pairs, calculated from the derivative assembly object. Typical values depend on genome size and completeness.
Length in base pairs of the largest contig in the SAG assembly, recorded as a contiguity metric for the computed genome reconstruction. Use the value derived from the final contig set.
N50 contig length in base pairs for the SAG assembly, calculated from the final contig set as a standard contiguity metric. Record the assembly-derived N50 value, not a process parameter.

Estimated completeness of the SAG assembly as a percentage, derived from the computed assembly using downstream assessment methods if integrated with the assembly result. Typical values range from 0 to 100.
Estimated contamination of the SAG assembly as a percentage, derived from the computed assembly result. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and indicate the fraction of non-target sequence detected.
Path, URI, or accession for the stored SAG assembly artifact, recorded as the location of the derived contig set. Example: '/data/assemblies/sample.fasta' or a repository accession string.
Checksum or hash for the assembly artifact used to verify file integrity and identity, recorded for the derived contig set. Example formats include MD5 or SHA256 digest strings.

Free-text scientific or technical notes describing notable characteristics of the computed assembly, such as fragmentation, suspected chimeras, or unusual contig structure, recorded as a derivative quality summary.

genome_annotation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only annotation workflow settings and the annotation software agent details, plus a process-level output summary. I excluded assembly properties because those belong to the upstream sag_assembly Derivative node, and I excluded gene/family feature outputs because those belong to the downstream annotated_genome_features Derivative node. I also followed the rule that software name, version, and repository belong on the Process node for computational steps. No already_generated list was provided here, so I stayed within the annotation process territory and avoided duplicating downstream feature annotations.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome annotation software used to predict genes and functional features from the SAG assembly, recorded for the computational annotation process. Example: 'Prokka', 'Prodigal', 'Bakta', or another annotation tool.
Version or release identifier of the annotation software used in this step, recorded at run time for reproducibility. Use the exact version string, such as '1.14.6' or a commit tag.

Repository location or reference for the annotation software used in the genome annotation process, recorded to identify the codebase. Example: a GitHub URL, package source, or internal repository identifier.

Name of the reference database used by the annotation pipeline to assign gene or function predictions, recorded during the annotation process. Example: 'KEGG', 'Pfam', 'NCBI nr', or a comparable resource.
Version or release date of the reference database used for genome annotation, recorded for reproducibility. Use the exact database version string if available.

Genetic code table used during gene prediction and annotation, recorded as a process parameter. Use the standard translation table identifier or descriptive label, for example the bacterial and archaeal code table.
E-value cutoff used for homology-based annotation or feature assignment, recorded as a numeric process parameter. Typical values are small, such as 1e-5 or 1e-10, depending on the pipeline.

Minimum amino-acid length required for predicted proteins or features to be retained in the annotation process, recorded as the filtering threshold used by the software. Typical values depend on the pipeline and genome context.

Categorical indicator summarizing the apparent success or reliability of the annotation run, recorded at the end of the annotation process. This is a process-level outcome, not the annotated feature set itself.
Free-text notes describing annotation-specific settings, database issues, or exceptions relevant to the computational process but not captured by structured fields.

annotated_genome_features.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed annotation-result properties: the annotated feature set identity/provenance, counts of predicted genes and functional elements, and artifact location/checksum plus lightweight result-quality notes. I excluded annotation software settings because those belong to the upstream genome_annotation Process, and I excluded assembly metrics because those belong to the upstream SAG assembly derivative. No already_generated list was provided here, so I kept the schema strictly in the derived annotation-result territory and avoided repeating process-level parameters.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed annotated feature set derived from the SAG assembly after genome annotation completes. Example format: 'annotated_features_0001'.
Identifier linking this annotated feature set back to the SAG assembly used as the annotation input. Use the parent assembly ID string, for example 'sag_assembly_0001'.
Total number of genes predicted in the annotated SAG genome, calculated from the derivative annotation result. This count should reflect the final annotated feature set.
Total number of coding sequences (CDS) predicted in the annotated SAG genome, calculated from the annotation output. Record the derivative count of CDS features.

Total number of rRNA features predicted in the annotated SAG genome, calculated from the annotation result. Typical bacterial and archaeal genomes may contain multiple rRNA operons depending on completeness.
Total number of tRNA features predicted in the annotated SAG genome, calculated from the annotation result. This is a derived feature count from the annotation output.

Total number of distinct functional categories or feature classes assigned in the annotated genome output, recorded as a summary of the derived annotation set. Examples include enzyme classes or pathway-related labels depending on pipeline output.
Path, URI, or accession for the stored annotated feature artifact, recorded as the location of the derived annotation output. Example: '/data/annotations/sample.gff' or a repository accession string.
Checksum or hash for the annotated feature file used to verify file integrity and identity, recorded for the derived annotation artifact. Example formats include MD5 or SHA256 digest strings.

Free-text notes describing notable characteristics of the annotated feature set, such as unusually low gene density, fragmented predictions, or other result-level observations relevant to the computed derivative.

assembly_quality_assessment.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the quality-assessment workflow settings, the software/tool identity, and process-level output summaries. I excluded assembly artifact properties because those belong to the upstream SAG assembly Derivative node, and I excluded the final metric file itself because that belongs to the downstream assembly_quality_metrics Derivative node. I also placed software name, version, and repository on the Process node as required for computational steps. No already_generated list was provided here, so I kept the schema within the quality-assessment process territory and avoided duplicating the actual derived metrics file.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to assess SAG assembly completeness, contamination, and related quality metrics, recorded for the computational quality-assessment process. Example: 'CheckM', 'CheckM2', 'BUSCO', or another tool.
Version or release identifier of the quality-assessment software used in this step, recorded at run time for reproducibility. Use the exact version string, such as '1.2.2' or a commit tag.

Repository location or reference for the quality-assessment software used in the computational process, recorded to identify the codebase. Example: a GitHub URL, package source, or internal repository identifier.

Categorical description of the approach used to evaluate the assembly, recorded during the quality assessment step. Use this to distinguish marker-gene, k-mer, coverage-based, or hybrid quality checks.

Name of the marker gene set or reference panel used for completeness and contamination estimation, recorded as a process parameter when applicable. Example: a domain-specific single-copy marker set name.

Completeness threshold in percent used by the quality-assessment workflow to classify or filter SAG assemblies, recorded as a process setting. Typical values may be 50, 70, or 90 depending on study design.
Contamination threshold in percent used by the quality-assessment workflow to classify or filter SAG assemblies, recorded as a process setting. Typical values are often low, such as 5 to 10 percent.
Categorical indicator summarizing whether the quality-assessment run completed successfully, partially, or failed, recorded at the end of the computational process.
Free-text notes describing special settings, exceptions, or observations during the quality-assessment process that are not captured by structured fields.

assembly_quality_metrics.reasoning: This is still the assembly_quality_metrics Derivative node, but I corrected the schema to avoid cross-DAG field collisions with already_generated fields. I removed source_sag_assembly_id, n50_bp, and largest_contig_length_bp because they were already produced elsewhere in the DAG. I kept only non-duplicating derived quality-summary fields that remain within this node's territory: metric object identity, provenance via an alternate non-colliding link, completeness/contamination/heterogeneity summaries, quality grade, and artifact storage integrity fields. I avoided upstream process settings and upstream assembly properties as before.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed assembly quality metrics object derived from the quality-assessment workflow. Example format: 'assembly_quality_metrics_0001'.

Reference linking this quality-metrics object back to the SAG assembly it summarizes, using an alternate field name to avoid duplication with previously generated identifiers. Record the parent assembly ID string here, for example 'sag_assembly_0001'.
Estimated completeness of the SAG assembly in percent, recorded as a computed quality metric after assessment. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and summarize recovery of expected genomic content.

Estimated contamination of the SAG assembly in percent, recorded as a computed quality metric after assessment. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and summarize non-target sequence detected in the assembly.

Estimated strain heterogeneity in percent, if computed by the quality-assessment workflow, recorded as a derived metric describing within-assembly variability. Use the output value reported by the assessment method when available.
Categorical summary grade assigned to the assembly based on the computed quality metrics, recorded for metadata-table use. Use the study's grading scheme if applicable.
Path, URI, or accession for the stored quality metrics artifact, recorded as the location of the derived metrics output. Example: '/data/metrics/sample_qc.json' or a repository accession string.
Checksum or hash for the quality metrics artifact used to verify file integrity and identity, recorded for the derived metrics output. Example formats include MD5 or SHA256 digest strings.
Boolean flag indicating whether the stored quality-metrics artifact passed integrity validation at ingestion, such as checksum verification or file readability checks.

metadata_integration.reasoning: This is a Process node that integrates downstream computed outputs into the final table, so I included only integration-workflow settings, join/mapping controls, table schema/format, and the software agent identity. I excluded upstream annotation and quality-metrics values themselves because those belong to the input Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final table contents because those belong to the downstream sag_metadata_table Derivative node. I also avoided reusing fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG, especially source linkage and common assembly metrics, and instead used integration-specific names that describe how the merge was performed.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, script, or pipeline used to merge annotation outputs and assembly quality metrics into the final SAG metadata table, recorded for this computational integration process. Example: 'pandas pipeline', 'R script', or a workflow name.
Version or release identifier of the integration software or script used in this step, recorded at run time for reproducibility. Use the exact version string or commit tag if available.

Repository location or reference for the integration code used to construct the final SAG table, recorded to identify the codebase. Example: a GitHub URL, package source, or internal repository identifier.

Categorical description of how the annotation and quality-metrics data were merged into the final metadata table. Use this to distinguish row-wise joining, key-based merging, or manual curation workflows.

Name of the table key or identifier field used to align annotation outputs with assembly quality metrics during integration. Provide the exact field name used in the workflow, for example a cell or assembly identifier string.
File or table format produced by the integration process before or during handoff to the final dataset table. Examples include CSV, TSV, JSON, or parquet, depending on the workflow.

Number of columns produced by the metadata integration process in the assembled SAG table, recorded as a process-level structural summary. Use the count after all selected annotation and quality fields have been merged.
Boolean flag indicating whether the integrated metadata table passed consistency checks during the integration process, such as key matching and column validation.

Free-text notes describing mapping decisions, join issues, missing values, or other details of the metadata integration workflow that are relevant to the process but not captured by structured fields.

sag_metadata_table.reasoning: This is the final Derivative node, so I included only table-level artifact properties: the table identity, its provenance back to the integration process, structure/size, storage location, checksum, and a compact content summary. I excluded upstream process and derivative values themselves because they belong to the contributing nodes already generated elsewhere in the DAG. I also avoided the previously reported collision-prone field names and used table-specific names instead. Since this node represents the final integrated dataset artifact, the fields focus on what a downstream user needs to locate, validate, and understand the table rather than on any single upstream step.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final integrated SAG metadata table artifact produced by the workflow. Example format: 'sag_metadata_table_0001'.

Identifier linking this metadata table back to the metadata integration process that produced it. Use the parent process or run ID string assigned by the workflow, for example 'metadata_integration_run_01'.

Number of rows in the final SAG metadata table, recorded for the integrated dataset artifact after construction. Use the final persisted table size, which typically corresponds to the number of SAG records.

Number of columns in the final SAG metadata table, recorded as a structural property of the integrated artifact. This should reflect the finalized table schema after all selected metadata fields have been merged.
File format of the final SAG metadata table artifact, recorded for the stored integrated dataset. Typical values include CSV, TSV, JSON, or parquet depending on the workflow output.

Path, URI, or accession for the stored final SAG metadata table, recorded as the location of the integrated derivative artifact. Example: '/data/final/sag_metadata_table.tsv' or a repository accession string.
Checksum or hash for the final metadata table used to verify file integrity and identity, recorded for the integrated dataset artifact. Example formats include MD5 or SHA256 digest strings.

Free-text summary of the kinds of metadata included in the final table, recorded at the dataset-artifact level. Briefly describe the major categories present, such as cell isolation, lysis, amplification, assembly, annotation, and quality fields.
Boolean flag indicating whether the final metadata table passed validation checks at publication or export time, such as schema conformity and row-level completeness checks.
